svg.title: What GA4 and server logs can each see
svg.desc: Two-column diagram of the method, no numbers. GA4's AI Assistant channel counts sessions that arrive with a referrer from a chatbot, so it counts people who clicked a link. It does not count an agent with no referrer or one that does not run the GA4 script, which can show as direct traffic or as a bot; that is the author's observation. Server or CDN logs count non-browser requests by user-agent and path, in a known-AI bucket and an unidentified automated bucket. The log alone cannot say the second bucket is an agent.
svg.text: WHAT EACH SOURCE CAN SEE
GA4 counts clicks from chatbots. Logs count requests.
GA4, AI Assistant channel
Server or CDN logs
Counts
Sessions that arrive with a referrer
from a chatbot: people who clicked
a link.
Misses
An agent with no referrer, or one that
never runs GA4's script. It can show as
direct or as a bot (my observation).
Counts
Non-browser requests per day, by
user-agent and path: a known-AI bucket
and an unidentified automated bucket.
Cannot tell
Whether the unidentified bucket is an
agent. It is a lead to investigate, not
a finding.
Method diagram, no data. Source: Google Analytics Help (channel definition).
The Misses and Cannot tell rows are the author's experience, not a published rule.
